newsitem.title: CHINA: China province to build gas-fired power plant.
newsitem.headline: China province to build gas-fired power plant.

text.p: China's southern Guangdong province plans to build a gas-fired power plant and a liquified gas storage centre to meet rising energy demand and limit pollution, the official Xinhua news agency said.

The provincial government, which had banned the construction of coal-fired power plants because of environmental problems, planned to build the 8,200 megawatt gas-fired plant in the Pearl River delta, it said.
Guangdong burned a total of 70 million tonnes of coal in 1995, 40 million tonnes of which was shipped in from elsewhere. The use of coal had led to serious environmental problems, Xinhua said.
The Guangdong government was considering importing liquified gas and planned to build a liquified gas storage centre, it added.
The province's current coastal gas supply would be unable to meet demand, which was expected to reach 4.0 billion cubic metres in 2000 and 6.0 billion cubic metres in 2010, Xinhua said.
